title: Day-to-Day Operations with AlmaLinux Desktop Experience

lessons.title: Plan Your Everyday Linux Desktop
lessons.description: Check hardware, backups, application needs, and a VM-first route before replacing your daily OS.

guide.where: AlmaLinux 9 GNOME desktop → Activities → Terminal, unless the step names Windows or VMware Workstation Pro.
guide.before: A Windows host with VMware Workstation Pro; no existing disks need changing.
guide.rollback: Keep using the existing OS; no disk or boot settings were changed.

steps.title: List what you need every day
steps.action: Write down browser, email, office documents, meetings, printers, games, VPN, and any Windows-only programs. Mark each as native Linux, web, or requires Windows.
steps.expect: You have a short compatibility checklist before installation.
steps.trouble: Do not assume Wine or Proton runs a work app, driver, or anti-cheat game.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: Your Windows host · lab notes and browser

steps.title: Choose the baseline
steps.action: Use the current supported AlmaLinux 9 x86_64 DVD ISO for this course and select Server with GUI during installation. The title says Server, but this profile supplies GNOME. AlmaLinux 10 may have different hardware and package support.
steps.expect: Your notes identify major version 9 and GNOME.
steps.trouble: Use official release notes to check CPU requirements; choose the image for your architecture.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: Your Windows host · lab notes and browser

steps.title: Protect your current machine
steps.action: Back up important files to a separate device or service and restore one sample. Save recovery keys for existing encrypted disks privately. Start with a new VM; do not repartition your Windows system.
steps.expect: The restored sample opens and the existing OS remains untouched.
steps.trouble: A VM snapshot is not a backup of the physical Windows disk.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: Your Windows host · lab notes and browser

steps.title: Size the practice VM
steps.action: Plan 2 virtual CPU cores, 4 GB RAM minimum for this exercise (8 GB if your host can spare it), a new 50 GB virtual disk, and NAT networking. Leave resources for Windows.
steps.expect: The host can run one GNOME VM without exhausting RAM or storage.
steps.trouble: These are lab sizing examples, not guarantees for every app or game.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: Your Windows host · lab notes and browser

steps.title: Plan a later physical installation
steps.action: Only after validating the VM, test a live environment if available and consult the current installation guide for Wi-Fi, audio, GPU, printers, encryption and disk layout. Keep backups and Windows recovery media.
steps.expect: You have a hardware test list and a recovery route.
steps.trouble: This course does not automatically convert or dual-boot an existing Windows installation.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: Your Windows host · lab notes and browser

guide.pass: Your checklist, verified backup, and VM plan are ready.

lessons.title: Install AlmaLinux with GNOME
lessons.description: Create a new Workstation VM and install AlmaLinux 9 Server with GUI.

guide.where: AlmaLinux 9 GNOME desktop → Activities → Terminal, unless the step names Windows or VMware Workstation Pro.
guide.before: Finish the desktop plan and obtain the official DVD ISO and its checksum.
guide.rollback: Delete only this new practice VM if rebuilding; leave host disks untouched.

steps.title: Verify the downloaded ISO
steps.action: Download the DVD ISO and CHECKSUM from almalinux.org using official mirror links. In Windows PowerShell compute its SHA-256 and compare with the exact filename in CHECKSUM; check official signature guidance when available. Replace the example ISO path in the command with the exact file you downloaded.
steps.expect: The complete SHA-256 matches the official checksum for your downloaded ISO.
steps.trouble: Do not use a checksum from an unrelated major version or file.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Create a fresh VM
steps.action: In VMware Workstation Pro choose File → New Virtual Machine → Typical → I will install the operating system later. Choose a compatible RHEL 9 64-bit guest profile (or AlmaLinux 9 if offered), name ALMA-DESKTOP, and create a NEW 50 GB virtual disk.
steps.expect: A new VM appears in the library with a blank disk.
steps.trouble: The VMware OS profile does not install the OS. Check Workstation compatibility if no suitable RHEL 9 profile is offered.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: Your Windows host · VMware Workstation Pro

steps.title: Attach media and networking
steps.action: Before power-on open VM Settings. Set 2 cores and your planned RAM. On CD/DVD attach the verified AlmaLinux 9 DVD ISO and enable Connect at power on. On Network Adapter select NAT.
steps.expect: The VM summary shows the correct ISO, memory, and NAT.
steps.trouble: Do not attach a physical WD disk or choose raw-disk access for this exercise.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: Your Windows host · VMware Workstation Pro

steps.title: Start the installer
steps.action: Power on and select Test this media & install AlmaLinux 9 if available. Choose your language, keyboard and time zone on Installation Summary.
steps.expect: You reach the installer summary without a media-check error.
steps.trouble: Check ISO checksum and attachment if it cannot boot; do not disable security settings at random.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Select GNOME and the correct disk
steps.action: Open Software Selection and choose Server with GUI. Open Installation Destination, select ONLY the new 50 GB virtual disk, and use automatic partitioning for this practice VM. Review any pending deletion list before accepting.
steps.expect: Only the new VM disk is selected and Server with GUI is the software profile.
steps.trouble: Stop if an existing disk or unexpected capacity appears. Cancel instead of deleting unknown partitions.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Create your daily user
steps.action: Open User Creation, choose your own username and strong password, and enable Make this user administrator (wheel privileges). Keep root credentials private if you set them. Enable the NAT interface in Network & Host Name, then begin installation.
steps.expect: The installer accepts a normal administrative user and completes.
steps.trouble: Do not use root as your everyday desktop login.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Boot the installed system
steps.action: Reboot when prompted, detach the ISO if it starts setup again, and sign in to GNOME as your normal user. Open Activities, search Terminal, and check the release.
steps.expect: The guest reports AlmaLinux 9 and opens a GNOME desktop.
steps.trouble: A text-only login often means a minimal profile was installed; for this new VM, reinstall with the required GUI profile.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

guide.pass: The VM boots from its disk into GNOME with your normal account.

lessons.title: Configure Your Desktop
lessons.description: Set display, keyboard, audio, privacy, updates, and VMware desktop integration.

guide.where: AlmaLinux 9 GNOME desktop → Activities → Terminal, unless the step names Windows or VMware Workstation Pro.
guide.before: A working AlmaLinux 9 GNOME VM and your normal user password.
guide.rollback: Restore the clean VM snapshot if appropriate; use Settings to reverse individual desktop choices.

steps.title: Set the basics
steps.action: Open Settings from the system menu. In Displays choose a readable resolution; in Keyboard/Region & Language verify layout; in Sound select output and test it. In Power choose sensible screen blanking.
steps.expect: Typing, display scaling and sound suit your setup.
steps.trouble: VM audio or resolution depends on Workstation settings and guest integration; do not install an unrelated GPU driver.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Confirm networking
steps.action: In Settings → Network check the wired connection. NAT normally supplies DHCP and DNS. Check addresses and routes without changing them.
steps.expect: You have an address and default route for the VM NAT connection.
steps.trouble: If disconnected, check Workstation Network Adapter → Connected before editing guest configuration.
steps.command:
ip -br address
ip route
nmcli device status
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Update the guest
steps.action: In Terminal refresh package metadata and review the proposed update transaction before accepting. Save work, then reboot when the update finishes.
steps.expect: The transaction completes without unresolved errors and GNOME returns after reboot.
steps.trouble: Check networking, free space and repositories if DNF fails; do not force-remove packages.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Install VMware desktop integration
steps.action: Inspect/install the distribution guest tools. Review the transaction, then log out and back in or reboot. Keep shared folders and host clipboard sharing off unless you intentionally need them.
steps.expect: GNOME can resize appropriately when supported by your Workstation settings.
steps.trouble: Do not use random third-party VMware Tools installers when distro packages are available.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Set lock and privacy
steps.action: In Settings → Privacy configure Screen Lock. Review Location and file-history options. Press Super+L and confirm the lock screen, then unlock with your own password.
steps.expect: The desktop locks and unlocks as expected.
steps.trouble: GNOME labels vary by minor version; search Settings for Screen Lock.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Record a clean baseline
steps.action: Open About and note release, memory and disk. Shut down the VM, then take a named Workstation snapshot if your edition supports it; separately keep backups of important files.
steps.expect: You have a starting point note and a VM recovery checkpoint.
steps.trouble: Snapshots depend on the VM disk and do not replace external backups.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: AlmaLinux VM · GNOME Settings; then VMware Workstation Pro on your host

guide.pass: Your desktop is updated, readable, connected, and locks properly.

lessons.title: Learn the Commands You Use Every Day
lessons.description: Practice navigation, files, help, search, pipes, and safe command habits in a practice folder.

guide.where: AlmaLinux 9 GNOME desktop → Activities → Terminal, unless the step names Windows or VMware Workstation Pro.
guide.before: GNOME Terminal, signed in as your own normal user.
guide.rollback: Keep or remove the practice folder through Files after checking its contents; no system files changed.

steps.title: Know where you are
steps.action: Open Terminal and check your identity and location. Read each command and output before moving on. ~ means your home directory, not the whole filesystem.
steps.expect: You recognize your own username, host and home path.
steps.trouble: If the account is root, close that session and return to your normal user.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Make a practice folder
steps.action: Create a practice folder under your home and move into it. mkdir -p creates missing parent directories. Use Tab to complete names and the Up arrow to recall a command.
steps.expect: pwd ends with DesktopPractice and the folder is inside your home.
steps.trouble: If you are elsewhere, return with cd ~; do not practice in /etc or /usr.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Create, copy and rename
steps.action: Write two lines to a practice text file. > replaces that named file; do not aim it at valuable files. Copy first, then rename the copy.
steps.expect: You have notes.txt and renamed.txt with the same two lines.
steps.trouble: Spaces in paths require quotes; Linux filenames are case-sensitive.
steps.command:
cd ~/DesktopPractice
printf "first line\nsecond line\n" > notes.txt
cp -i notes.txt copy.txt
mv -i copy.txt renamed.txt
cat renamed.txt
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Search and inspect
steps.action: Find files and filter text. A pipe sends one command’s output into the next. Use less to page through longer output and press q to leave.
steps.expect: grep returns the matching line and wc counts two lines.
steps.trouble: No grep match is not a system failure; verify the exact text.
steps.command:
cd ~/DesktopPractice
grep -n "second" notes.txt
wc -l notes.txt
find . -maxdepth 1 -type f
ls -lah | less
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Learn help and interruption
steps.action: Use --help or man for syntax; q exits man. Ctrl+C interrupts a foreground task; Ctrl+Shift+C copies selected text in GNOME Terminal. Never paste a command you cannot explain.
steps.expect: You can find an option’s meaning and exit a pager.
steps.trouble: If man is missing install man-db through DNF after reviewing the transaction.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Clean only your practice copy
steps.action: Use interactive removal for the renamed practice copy. Confirm only after checking its full path, then verify the original remains. Avoid rm -rf as a routine cleanup habit.
steps.expect: notes.txt remains and the chosen practice copy is gone.
steps.trouble: Do not add sudo or wildcard paths to fix a typo.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

guide.pass: You can navigate, check, create, copy, search and remove a practice file without sudo.

lessons.title: Manage Files and Permissions
lessons.description: Use Files, archives, removable media, permissions, and everyday keyboard shortcuts.

guide.where: AlmaLinux 9 GNOME desktop → Activities → Terminal, unless the step names Windows or VMware Workstation Pro.
guide.before: Complete the command practice and keep its notes.txt sample.
guide.rollback: Restore a practice file from Trash or extract the archive; reverse only the specific permission change if needed.

steps.title: Navigate with Files
steps.action: Open Files from Activities. Open Home, Documents and Downloads. Ctrl+L enters a path; type ~/DesktopPractice and Enter. Ctrl+H toggles hidden files.
steps.expect: You can locate the same practice file from GUI and Terminal.
steps.trouble: Hidden files often store configuration; do not delete them to tidy the home directory.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Create and organize
steps.action: In Files create an Everyday folder in Documents. Copy notes.txt into it, rename the copy, and open it with the text editor. Use Trash for unwanted practice copies.
steps.expect: Your copied document opens and the original is still present.
steps.trouble: Moving within a disk and copying to a different disk have different space effects; confirm the destination.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Understand permissions
steps.action: Check a file you own. Apply mode 600 to the practice notes only: owner read/write, no access for group/others. This is not full-disk encryption.
steps.expect: ls shows owner-only read/write on that practice file.
steps.trouble: Do not use chmod 777 or recursively change your entire home to fix one app.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Create an archive
steps.action: Use Files → right-click the Everyday folder → Compress (menu labels can vary). Choose a ZIP filename. Extract it into a temporary folder and open the copied note.
steps.expect: The extracted note matches your original.
steps.trouble: An archive on the same disk is convenient packaging, not an independent backup.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Use removable storage
steps.action: Connect a USB data drive and open its entry in Files. Copy a harmless sample, wait for transfer completion, then use Eject/Unmount before disconnecting.
steps.expect: The sample reopens and the drive disconnects without a busy warning.
steps.trouble: In VMware use VM → Removable Devices to intentionally connect a USB device to the guest; the host loses access while attached.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

guide.pass: You can find, organize, archive and move your own files and explain owner permissions.

lessons.title: Install and Maintain Everyday Apps
lessons.description: Use DNF and user-scoped Flatpak to install trusted desktop apps and keep them updated.

guide.where: AlmaLinux 9 GNOME desktop → Activities → Terminal, unless the step names Windows or VMware Workstation Pro.
guide.before: Updated AlmaLinux 9 desktop; understand that adding a third-party app source is a trust choice.
guide.rollback: Use sudo dnf remove libreoffice or flatpak uninstall --user org.videolan.VLC only after reviewing the removal plan; preserve documents separately.

steps.title: Inspect your existing software sources
steps.action: DNF manages system RPMs and dependencies. GNOME Software may show RPM and Flatpak sources. List enabled DNF repositories and check package details before installing.
steps.expect: You know which repositories are currently enabled.
steps.trouble: A missing package is not a reason to run an unknown curl-to-shell installer.
steps.command:
dnf repolist
dnf info firefox
dnf search libreoffice
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Install a native everyday app
steps.action: For an office suite use the AlmaLinux repository package libreoffice if available. Read the package source, extra packages the app needs and download size, then approve the install. Start it from Activities.
steps.expect: A document opens in the installed app.
steps.trouble: If unavailable, stop and check repository configuration or choose the Flatpak alternative; do not mix RPMs for another distro.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Install Flatpak support
steps.action: Install the Flatpak client from your configured AlmaLinux repositories. Then check existing user remotes. System and user remotes are different scopes.
steps.expect: flatpak is available and your user remote list is visible.
steps.trouble: Restart your login session after adding desktop integration if new app launchers do not appear.
steps.command:
sudo dnf install flatpak
flatpak --version
flatpak remotes --user
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Add Flathub only after reviewing the source
steps.action: Open the official Flathub AlmaLinux setup page linked below. If you accept this third-party source, add it to your user only. Check its URL afterward.
steps.expect: The user-scoped flathub remote points to the official source.
steps.trouble: Do not disable signature checking. A store listing is not a guarantee that every publisher or permission is appropriate.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: AlmaLinux VM · web browser for Flathub; then GNOME Terminal

steps.title: Install an app and review permissions
steps.action: Search for VLC, check the exact Flathub app ID and source, then install the user-scoped example only if you accept its publisher and permissions. Launch from Activities or Terminal.
steps.expect: VLC starts and opens a non-sensitive local media sample.
steps.trouble: Codec availability and licenses vary. Do not enable every third-party repository just to make one format play.
steps.command:
flatpak search VLC
flatpak remote-info --user flathub org.videolan.VLC
flatpak install --user flathub org.videolan.VLC
flatpak info --user --show-permissions org.videolan.VLC
flatpak run org.videolan.VLC
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Update and remove deliberately
steps.action: Update RPMs with DNF and user Flatpaks separately. Before removing an app, review extra packages the app needs and preserve needed data. Flatpak uninstall without --delete-data normally leaves user app data.
steps.expect: You can explain the two update paths and identify an app’s source.
steps.trouble: Do not accept a removal transaction that unexpectedly removes your desktop.
steps.command:
sudo dnf upgrade --refresh
flatpak update --user
flatpak list --user --app
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

guide.pass: You installed and launched an app, inspected its source and permissions, and know how it updates.

lessons.title: Install Steam and Understand Proton
lessons.description: Install Steam, test one supported game, and understand GPU, Proton, and anti-cheat limits.

guide.where: AlmaLinux 9 GNOME desktop → Activities → Terminal, unless the step names Windows or VMware Workstation Pro.
guide.before: Complete Flatpak setup; a Steam account and a game you legitimately own or a free native game. A VM is for setup practice, not a gaming performance promise.
guide.rollback: Remove only the test game using Steam’s Manage/Uninstall; back up saves first. Uninstalling Steam does not guarantee all game data is removed.

steps.title: Check hardware and game support first
steps.action: Read the game’s official Linux/Steam requirements. Check GPU support and the current Steam/Proton information. Anti-cheat, DRM and Windows-only launchers may prevent play; some games require Windows.
steps.expect: You selected one compatible test title and recorded the hardware expectation.
steps.trouble: A VMware virtual GPU is not your full physical GPU. Install/setup success in a VM does not prove a modern 3D game will work.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: Your Windows host · lab notes and browser

steps.title: Inspect and install Steam from Flathub
steps.action: Check the exact Steam application ID on Flathub and its permissions. The Flatpak wrapper is community maintained. Review requirements and accept the install only if it fits your system.
steps.expect: Steam is installed in your user Flatpak scope.
steps.trouble: If the app reports unsupported architecture or missing runtime support, stop and review current Flathub requirements.
steps.command:
flatpak remote-info --user flathub com.valvesoftware.Steam
flatpak install --user flathub com.valvesoftware.Steam
flatpak info --user --show-permissions com.valvesoftware.Steam
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Start and sign in
steps.action: Launch Steam from Activities or Terminal and let its client updates finish. Sign in privately; never capture the password, QR code or Steam Guard code for evidence.
steps.expect: You reach your own Steam Library.
steps.trouble: Do not install an untrusted launcher or bypass account security to work around a sign-in error.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Try a native title first
steps.action: Choose a small Linux-native title that meets the VM or physical machine’s graphics capability. Pick the default library location, check required space, and download it. Launch and record the actual result.
steps.expect: The supported test game launches, or you record the specific compatibility failure.
steps.trouble: A driver error needs hardware-specific vendor guidance. Do not disable SELinux or install random graphics-driver scripts.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Test Proton separately
steps.action: In Steam → Settings → Compatibility check Steam Play/Proton options. For a compatible Windows title, use its Properties → Compatibility to choose an offered supported Proton version when needed. Test one title at a time.
steps.expect: You can distinguish native Linux execution from a Windows game using Proton.
steps.trouble: Not every title works. Check official game/anti-cheat support; community ProtonDB reports are supporting clues, not guarantees.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Keep libraries and runtimes healthy
steps.action: Update user Flatpaks and Steam. Use Steam Settings → Storage to view library usage. For an external library first complete the WD storage class and grant only that path to the Steam sandbox.
steps.expect: You know where the game is stored and how much free space remains.
steps.trouble: Use a Linux-native filesystem for this lab’s Steam library. NTFS permissions, compatibility layers and sandbox paths can cause failures.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

guide.pass: Steam opens and you can report an actual game result with its compatibility constraints.

lessons.title: Configure Network, Printing and Sharing
lessons.description: Check Wi-Fi or Ethernet, DNS, printers, Bluetooth, and file-sharing access.

guide.where: AlmaLinux 9 GNOME desktop → Activities → Terminal, unless the step names Windows or VMware Workstation Pro.
guide.before: GNOME desktop and a network/printer you are allowed to use.
guide.rollback: Remove only the test printer/pairing/mount and restore any connection setting you recorded before changing it.

steps.title: Inspect network before changing it
steps.action: Use Settings → Network or Wi-Fi for your connection. A VMware VM usually sees virtual Ethernet even when Windows uses Wi-Fi. Check active connections and addresses.
steps.expect: You identify the right adapter and active connection.
steps.trouble: Do not copy your physical Wi-Fi static IP into a NAT guest.
steps.command:
nmcli connection show --active
ip -br address
ip route
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Separate DNS from connectivity
steps.action: Resolve a known official site, then test HTTPS. If name lookup fails but your network route exists, check the connection’s DNS details before changing anything.
steps.expect: You can tell a name-resolution error from an HTTPS or connection error.
steps.trouble: Do not replace required VPN/domain DNS with public DNS without understanding the network.
steps.command:
getent hosts almalinux.org
curl -I https://almalinux.org
nmcli device show
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Add a printer
steps.action: Open Settings → Printers, unlock if requested, choose Add, and select an allowed detected printer or its confirmed IPP address. Print a single test page.
steps.expect: The queue exists and the actual test page prints.
steps.trouble: Discovery across NAT/VPN may not work. Use the printer’s official IPP/driver guidance; availability depends on the hardware.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Configure peripherals
steps.action: In Settings → Bluetooth pair one device if supported. Test input/output under Sound. In a VM pass through a specific USB device only when needed, then disconnect it when finished.
steps.expect: The chosen device works, or its unsupported state is documented.
steps.trouble: A VM may have no Bluetooth adapter. Do not assume the host’s device automatically exists in the guest.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Access a known file share
steps.action: In Files → Other Locations enter the approved smb://server/share address. Use an account authorized for that share and test with a harmless file. Disconnect afterward.
steps.expect: The authorized share opens without changing server permissions.
steps.trouble: A credential prompt does not mean a public share. Do not make the entire home directory world-writable to solve access.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

guide.pass: You verified network/DNS and tested at least one available peripheral or authorized share.

lessons.title: Add Storage from a Western Digital Drive
lessons.description: Identify a WD drive, mount existing files safely, and prepare a separate empty practice disk.

guide.where: AlmaLinux 9 GNOME desktop → Activities → Terminal, unless the step names Windows or VMware Workstation Pro.
guide.before: Back up the WD drive elsewhere and verify a restore. Know whether it is USB/external or internal, its model/serial/capacity, filesystem, and whether it contains files to keep.
guide.rollback: Unmount the data volume. Revert only its recorded mount-option changes; formatting has no simple undo and requires restoration from a separate backup.

steps.title: Identify how the drive reaches AlmaLinux
steps.action: On a physical AlmaLinux PC connect the intended USB drive, or power off and follow the PC manual for an internal SATA installation. In VMware, USB passthrough can attach an external disk exclusively to the guest. For learning, prefer adding a separate NEW virtual disk while powered off. Never use raw access to your Windows system disk.
steps.expect: The drive appears in AlmaLinux without formatting or partition changes.
steps.trouble: A WD drive mounted in Windows is not automatically a Linux block device inside VMware. Disconnect/eject safely before switching ownership.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: Your Windows host · VMware Workstation Pro

steps.title: Match model, serial and capacity
steps.action: Open Activities → Disks. Select the candidate drive and record its model, serial, size and partitions. Compare with the physical device label. Check terminal output too; do not assume /dev/sdb is always the WD drive.
steps.expect: You positively distinguish the data drive from the system disk mounted at /.
steps.trouble: Stop if USB bridge hides serial/model or the device identity is ambiguous.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Use an existing data volume without erasing it
steps.action: If it contains files, select its existing partition in Disks and use Mount (play button), or open it from Files. Do NOT choose Format Disk, Format Partition or Delete. Record the actual mount path from Disks and check your own files.
steps.expect: Existing files are visible and unchanged.
steps.trouble: If encrypted, unlock with your own key; if filesystem support is missing, follow official AlmaLinux support guidance. NTFS from hibernated/Fast Startup Windows can be unsafe to write: return to Windows for a full shutdown. Never force a read/write mount.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Prove copy access and available space
steps.action: For a writable mounted volume copy only your harmless notes.txt using Files, reopen it, and compare its SHA-256 with the source. In Terminal quote the ACTUAL mounted path when using df -h or findmnt -T. Do not run a placeholder as a path.
steps.expect: The sample file matches and free space is shown for that mounted filesystem.
steps.trouble: NTFS/exFAT ownership is controlled by mount options; chown is not a universal fix. Never recursively chmod a valuable drive.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Optional: prepare a NEW empty practice disk
steps.action: Skip this step for any drive containing data. On a separate practice blank virtual disk, reconfirm identity in Disks, use its menu → Format Disk → GPT if a partition table is needed, then the + button → Create Partition → choose ext4 for Linux-only practice and a label such as PracticeData. Formatting ERASES selected content; review the device and deletion prompts before confirming.
steps.expect: Only the explicitly empty practice disk has the new Linux filesystem.
steps.trouble: If you cannot prove the device is empty and practice, stop. A WD brand label is not authorization to erase it. Use the existing-volume route instead.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Choose persistent mounting only if needed
steps.action: Existing removable drives can simply mount from Files when plugged in. For a dedicated Linux data disk, in Disks select the partition → gear → Edit Mount Options; record the existing options, use stable UUID identification, a deliberate path such as /mnt/WDData, and nofail for an optional disk. Test while attached before a reboot. Do not edit the root mount.
steps.expect: The chosen data volume mounts at its intended path and the machine still boots.
steps.trouble: Do not add a guessed UUID or device name to /etc/fstab. Permission options depend on the filesystem. If boot is affected, revert this data-volume mount entry using your recovery route.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Understand what space you added
steps.action: A disk mounted at /mnt/WDData increases storage available at that path; it does not enlarge /. Keep files there intentionally. On a new empty ext4 practice mount only, use Files as an administrator or a reviewed one-directory ownership change for your user; never recursively chown an existing data tree.
steps.expect: You can explain which filesystem gains files and which remains unchanged.
steps.trouble: Growing root or LVM is a different task requiring the actual disk/partition layout and a tested backup; do not run generic resize commands.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Use it for games or disconnect it safely
steps.action: For Steam use a Linux-native dedicated library folder on this mounted drive. Grant only that ACTUAL folder to the user Steam Flatpak (via a permissions manager or reviewed flatpak override --user --filesystem=EXACT_PATH com.valvesoftware.Steam), then add the library in Steam Settings → Storage. When done close apps and unmount/eject before unplugging.
steps.expect: The correct library path is visible, or the data volume ejects cleanly.
steps.trouble: Never grant all host files just for one game. Revoke the same path permission when no longer needed. A busy mount means an app still uses it.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

guide.pass: You identified the WD device, preserved existing files, and verified a mount and sample copy. Formatting is optional and restricted to an empty practice disk.

lessons.title: Back Up Your Desktop and Restore a File
lessons.description: Create an independent backup of everyday files and prove recovery by restoring a sample.

guide.where: AlmaLinux 9 GNOME desktop → Activities → Terminal, unless the step names Windows or VMware Workstation Pro.
guide.before: A second storage device or approved backup destination with enough space; practice notes.txt exists.
guide.rollback: Keep the source files until restored data is verified; do not delete the only backup.

steps.title: Choose what matters
steps.action: List Documents, Pictures, project files, browser exports and game saves you need. Include needed hidden app data deliberately. Do not assume an installed app is the same as its documents.
steps.expect: You have a short backup scope and destination.
steps.trouble: Never put passwords or private keys into an unencrypted shared folder.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: Your Windows host · lab notes and browser

steps.title: Make a dated sample backup
steps.action: In Files create a dated backup folder on your verified external destination. Copy the Everyday folder and practice notes. Wait for completion, then safely unmount the destination.
steps.expect: The copied files exist on a different device.
steps.trouble: A folder on the same physical disk does not protect against that disk failing.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Prove restore without overwriting
steps.action: Reconnect the destination and copy the sample into ~/RestoreTest using Files. Open it and compare hashes for the original and restored file.
steps.expect: Restored content matches and opens.
steps.trouble: Do not overwrite the only original while learning to restore.
steps.command:
sha256sum ~/DesktopPractice/notes.txt
# Also hash your actual restored file path; compare the full values.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Schedule a repeatable habit
steps.action: For this first class, use the manual Files backup you just tested. Set a weekly reminder in your calendar to copy the chosen folders into a new dated folder on your backup drive. Keep earlier copies until you check the new one. Write down when you last restored a sample, where the backup lives and who can unlock any encryption. You can choose an automated backup tool later; do not call a scheduled copy a tested backup until you have restored from it.
steps.expect: Your plan says when to back up and how to recover.
steps.trouble: A sync service can replicate deletion; check its version and restore behavior.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: AlmaLinux VM · backup notes and calendar

steps.title: Keep VM snapshots separate
steps.action: Use powered-off VM snapshots for short experiment rollback, and separate backups for valuable data. Review snapshot growth and remove obsolete snapshots using Workstation’s supported manager.
steps.expect: You can explain rollback versus independent file recovery.
steps.trouble: Do not delete VMDK files manually to clean snapshots.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: Your Windows host · VMware Workstation Pro

guide.pass: One independent backup and a successful sample restore are documented.

lessons.title: Troubleshoot Everyday Linux Problems
lessons.description: Diagnose slow apps, full storage, service errors, and SELinux denials without disabling protections.

guide.where: AlmaLinux 9 GNOME desktop → Activities → Terminal, unless the step names Windows or VMware Workstation Pro.
guide.before: Normal user terminal and a known-good starting point; no fault injection required.
guide.rollback: Restore the specific saved configuration or a known-good practice-VM backup.

steps.title: State the problem precisely
steps.action: Record what failed, when, the app, the last change, and whether it happens to all users or one. Reproduce using a harmless action and capture the exact error.
steps.expect: You have one testable problem statement.
steps.trouble: Avoid changing network, drivers and permissions simultaneously.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Check resources
steps.action: Check space, memory and running processes. In top press q to exit. A full filesystem can break updates and app state.
steps.expect: You can identify the filesystem or process actually consuming resources.
steps.trouble: Do not delete /var, package databases, or unknown system files to free space.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Inspect services and recent errors
steps.action: Read failed units and the current boot’s warning/error journal. Journal access can require authorized sudo; check before changing a service.
steps.expect: You can relate an error timestamp and service to the symptom.
steps.trouble: Failed units can be unrelated to your app. Never restart arbitrary services simply to clear the list.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Inspect one service deliberately
steps.action: For an actual named failed service, use systemctl status SERVICE and journalctl -u SERVICE -b. Replace SERVICE with the real unit from your previous check. Research the specific error before a restart.
steps.expect: You know the failing dependency/configuration or what saved result is missing.
steps.trouble: The word SERVICE is a placeholder. A restart changes state and may interrupt other work.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Respect SELinux and firewall boundaries
steps.action: Check SELinux state and active firewall policy. If an app is denied, check its logs and the official supported labeling/port guidance. Do not disable SELinux or firewalld as the default workaround.
steps.expect: You recorded current protection state without weakening it.
steps.trouble: A Flatpak sandbox permission problem differs from an SELinux denial; check the app’s scope first.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Recover and prove the fix
steps.action: Reverse only the identified change, restore an app config backup, or use the VM recovery checkpoint if necessary. Repeat the original test and save before/after evidence.
steps.expect: The original problem is resolved or narrowed with clear next evidence.
steps.trouble: Package downgrades and dnf history undo can fail when old packages are unavailable; a tested backup is the recovery plan.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

guide.pass: You can work from symptom → saved result → one change → retest without disabling protections.

lessons.title: Connect to Real AlmaLinux Terminal Output
lessons.description: Run the local SONIC companion and verify real PowerShell output, then reach AlmaLinux with SSH or its native Terminal.

guide.where: AlmaLinux 9 GNOME desktop → Activities → Terminal, unless the step names Windows or VMware Workstation Pro.
guide.before: Your Windows workstation with Git, Node.js 22.13+ and npm, the SONIC repository, and the AlmaLinux VM. Run the companion as your normal Windows user.
guide.rollback: Disconnect, stop the companion, and remove any SSH firewall exception you intentionally added if no longer required; keep GNOME Terminal for local work.

steps.title: Understand where commands execute
steps.action: The hosted website is copy/help mode. GNOME Terminal runs Bash inside your AlmaLinux VM. The local SONIC companion starts PowerShell on Windows; its WSL tab is a separately installed WSL distro, NOT your VMware VM.
steps.expect: You can name the machine each shell controls.
steps.trouble: Real commands need an actual shell. Changing text in the dashboard does not create a terminal backend.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: Your Windows host · lab notes and browser

steps.title: Install Node.js and Git, then start the local app
steps.action: On your Windows host, open Start, type Windows PowerShell and open it. Follow the linked terminal setup guide to install Node.js LTS (which includes npm) and Git with its PowerShell commands. Close and reopen PowerShell or use the guide’s PATH refresh command. Run node --version, npm.cmd --version and git --version before continuing. In File Explorer, open the downloaded academy project folder, click its address bar, type powershell and press Enter: that opens PowerShell in the correct project folder. Run the block below there; npm.cmd avoids a blocked npm.ps1 script without weakening your execution policy.
steps.expect: SONIC opens on localhost, normally port 3000.
steps.trouble: If node or git is not recognized, reopen PowerShell after installation and check the installer PATH option. npm is bundled with Node.js. Use npm.cmd if PowerShell blocks npm.ps1; do not lower the execution policy to work around it.
steps.command:
Set-Location $env:USERPROFILE
git clone --branch main https://github.com/CloudSeamTech/SONIC-Academy.git
Set-Location .\SONIC-Academy
npm.cmd ci
npm.cmd run dev
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Start the companion in a second Windows window
steps.action: From the same repository root in a second PowerShell window install the packages the companion needs and start it. Keep this process open. The random pairing token is private and stays on your computer.
steps.expect: The companion prints a loopback address and pairing token.
steps.trouble: node-pty may require Visual Studio Build Tools Desktop development with C++ and Python if no matching native binary is available. Follow the actual installation error; do not disable security software.
steps.command:
npm.cmd run companion:install
npm.cmd run companion:start
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Connect and prove a real Windows result
steps.action: At http://localhost:3000/migration#view=terminal select Windows PowerShell. Paste the token into the local-only field and Connect locally. Run Get-Date twice. Compare with your own Windows clock.
steps.expect: Live date/time output appears from your current Windows account.
steps.trouble: Do not paste the token into the hosted site, a URL or a screenshot. If unavailable, check companion startup/capability errors.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: Your Windows host · web browser at http://localhost:3000/migration#view=terminal

steps.title: Optionally enable SSH inside the AlmaLinux guest
steps.action: For VMware access use GNOME Terminal to install/start the SSH server and check its address and firewall. If SSH is not already allowed, add the ssh service only to the active connection’s firewall zone after checking it. This opens private-network SSH access; NAT needs no public port-forward. In firewall-config select the active zone and check the ssh service only for that private connection, then make the reviewed change permanent if needed. Alternatively use firewall-cmd --zone=<your-active-zone> --add-service=ssh, replacing the placeholder; repeat with --permanent only after testing.
steps.expect: sshd is active and you know the guest’s actual NAT address.
steps.trouble: Do not open public port 22 or disable the firewall. If you only need local desktop commands, GNOME Terminal requires no SSH server.
steps.command:
sudo dnf install openssh-server
sudo systemctl enable --now sshd
ip -br address
sudo firewall-cmd --get-active-zones
sudo firewall-cmd --list-all
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.

steps.title: Verify host identity and connect from Windows
steps.action: In the guest check the ED25519 host-key fingerprint. In Windows PowerShell use ssh your-user@the-actual-guest-IP and compare the offered fingerprint before accepting. The text user/IP are placeholders; substitute your own. Use native PowerShell for a full interactive SSH session; the SONIC panel can relay basic prompts but is not a full-screen terminal emulator.
steps.expect: You reach the intended AlmaLinux host and can verify its release and username.
steps.trouble: If SSH is blocked, review the active firewall zone and Workstation NAT route. Never ignore a changed host-key warning.
steps.command:
sudo ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub
# Above: AlmaLinux guest only. Then run ssh with your actual user/IP in Windows.
# After SSH connects: whoami; hostname; cat /etc/os-release
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: AlmaLinux VM · Terminal; then Windows host · PowerShell

steps.title: Use the right terminal and shut down cleanly
steps.action: Run AlmaLinux desktop commands in GNOME Terminal or your verified SSH session. Use exit to leave SSH. In SONIC choose Disconnect and stop the companion process with Ctrl+C when finished. Stop the local dev server separately.
steps.expect: Remote/local prompts are distinguishable and the companion is no longer listening when stopped.
steps.trouble: The risk labels are guidance, not a sandbox: commands execute with your real account permissions. Do not run destructive drive commands just to test output.
steps.evidence: Save your own screenshot or notes showing the target, action, and observed result. Exclude passwords and private information.
steps.where: AlmaLinux VM · GNOME Terminal; then local academy browser on your Windows host

guide.pass: You observed real Get-Date output and can identify the Windows, WSL and VMware AlmaLinux execution contexts. SSH is optional and checked against the guest fingerprint.
